source: Microsoft WinDbg built-in MCP after operator disconnected the baseline controller, reconnected it and reported allocation breakpoint hit
condition: PID initialization supplied for the first GameInput queue entry in a fresh device context

guard_checks: both list-head links identify empty list

interpretation: The corrected fresh-device list remained at one entry through observed reuse and the short resumed interval. The earlier uncorrected fresh-device list grew from one to 332. This supports missing PID initialization as the cause of excess queue creation in this configuration.
limitations: Single pair of serial VM runs with approximate host timing, not exact matched guest execution durations or an allocation-rate measurement.
Hands-off input was requested but not independently measured; other guest process activity was not exhaustively controlled.
Retired device objects remained after disconnect; complete teardown and equal retired-device residency were not established.
The one-node correction covers the observed GameInput requestor; it is not a driver-code patch or a fix for all processes.
The corrected PID remains present in the current device lifetime. No existing queues were forcibly removed and no services changed.
No corrected handle-close benchmark, game frame-time, input/vibration fidelity or recovery result is yet available.
The guest inbox revision differs from the contributor's later revision; do not generalize to other Windows or GameInput builds.
